The organization's SAML SingleSignOnService over the HTTP-Redirect binding, with Qeet acting as the Identity Provider. It handles SP-initiated SSO from the AuthnRequest of a Service Provider registered in that organization and IdP-initiated SSO by SP reference; only SPs of the organization in the path are matched. The user is authenticated by the hosted-login SSO cookie, and the browser is bounced to the hosted login when no session exists. On success it returns an auto-submitting HTML form that POSTs a signed SAMLResponse to the SP's registered ACS URL. Only people whose home is the organization are signed in (403 saml.user_organization_mismatch otherwise), and an SP with assignment_required only those assigned to it, themselves or through a group of the organization they belong to: anyone else is refused with 403 saml.sp_not_assigned, and the refusal is audited as saml.idp_assertion_refused. The assertion's NameID follows the SP's name_id_format and name_id_attribute (an emailAddress NameID is the email; a persistent one an opaque value made for this person at this SP the first time they sign in to it, which never changes, or their user id when name_id_attribute is user_id); a NameID from a metadata key the person has no single value for is refused with 403 saml.name_id_unavailable, also audited. The assertion carries the attributes the SP maps, each the person has a value for. A browser asking for HTML gets every error as a page showing its message and code; anything else gets the JSON error. An unknown or inactive organization, or an unknown SP, returns 404; a disabled SP answers 403 saml.service_provider_disabled, and one still in draft 403 saml.service_provider_draft, whether or not anyone is signed in (a signed-in person's attempt is audited as saml.idp_assertion_refused, reason draft). The organization's plan must include enterprise SSO at every sign-in, not only when the SP was registered (402 billing.upgrade_required). As at OIDC authorize, the organization's address rules apply (403 auth.address_not_allowed, recorded as auth.address_refused with path saml_idp), and so does its second-factor requirement: a session whose sign-in didn't meet it is sent to sign in again (302 to the hosted login's /sign-in with prompt=login, returning here marked with login_after), and a fresh sign-in that still hasn't is refused with 403 step_up_required or mfa.enrollment_required, audited as saml.idp_assertion_refused with reason second_factor_required. An SP with require_signed_requests is signed in only by a request signed with its certificate, over the query as the Redirect binding defines (RSA or ECDSA with SHA-256 or SHA-512) or by an enveloped XML signature, and is otherwise refused with 403 saml.request_signature_invalid, as is a Redirect-binding query that gives SAMLRequest, RelayState, SigAlg or Signature twice or under a percent-encoded name; IdP-initiated sign-in is unaffected. An SP with encrypt_assertions gets the signed assertion as an EncryptedAssertion to its certificate. The POST-binding variant is POST /saml/idp/{organizationID}/sso.
(Required) The organization's ID. On an authenticated route it must be the organization of the caller's credential: another is refused with 403, and a value that is not a UUID with 400.

description.content: Creates an inbound SAML connection in the organization with the external IdP's entity id, SSO URL and signing certificate so Qeet can act as the Service Provider for that IdP. A name alone creates a draft before the IdP's details are known, since the IdP needs the connection's addresses first: the answer carries them (sp_entity_id, acs_url, sp_metadata_url), and the IdP's details are added later by PATCH, its metadata or its certificates. Any one of the IdP's details brings the rest with it (422 saml.connection_fields_required), and a connection without them is a draft only (422 saml.connection_incomplete). Validate the configuration with the connection test endpoint, then drive sign-in via GET /saml/login/{id}. Scoped to the organization in the path. description.content: Registers a downstream Service Provider in the organization, including its entity id, ACS URL and NameID format, so it can obtain signed assertions from Qeet acting as the Identity Provider. Registered SPs are matched by AuthnRequest issuer or SP reference at the organization's IdP SSO endpoint, /saml/idp/{organizationID}/sso; the entity id need be unique only within the organization. Give the SP administrator the organization's IdP metadata from /saml/idp/{organizationID}/metadata to complete the trust. The ACS URL, where signed assertions are posted, must be an absolute https URL without user information (plain http only to localhost), or the answer is 422 saml.acs_url_invalid. A status, when given, must be draft, active or disabled (422 saml.status_invalid), and an entity id already registered in the organization is refused with 409 saml.sp_entity_id_taken. The NameID format is emailAddress (the default), persistent or unspecified (422 saml.name_id_format_invalid otherwise), and name_id_attribute names where its value comes from: email, user_id, persistent_id (an opaque value made for each person at this SP, which never changes) or metadata.<key>. An emailAddress NameID is always the email and a persistent one persistent_id (its default) or user_id; another combination is refused with 422 saml.name_id_attribute_invalid. attributes, when given, replaces the default email and name attributes; an empty list sends none, and an invalid one is refused with 422 saml.attributes_invalid naming each field at fault. assignment_required limits sign-in to the people and groups assigned to the SP. The registration is audited as saml.sp_created with these settings.
(Required) The organization's ID. On an authenticated route it must be the organization of the caller's credential: another is refused with 403, and a value that is not a UUID with 400.

Creates an inbound SAML connection from the external IdP's SAML 2.0 metadata, given either as the XML (metadata_xml) or as a URL to fetch it from (metadata_url). The connection takes the IdP's entity id, its https HTTP-Redirect SingleSignOnService and its signing certificates from the metadata. A connection given a URL refreshes from it every few hours, adding the IdP's new signing certificates and dropping those the metadata no longer lists (certificates an administrator added are kept); metadata that can't be fetched or no longer describes the same IdP changes nothing and is reported in metadata_error. The URL is fetched only from public https addresses, with a 10-second timeout and a 1 MiB limit. Metadata describing several identity providers needs idp_entity_id to pick one. Neither or both sources answer 422 saml.metadata_required; unusable metadata 422 saml.metadata_invalid, with the reason in detail; a URL that isn't allowed 422 saml.metadata_url_invalid; one that can't be fetched 422 saml.metadata_unreachable. The organization's plan must include enterprise SSO (402 billing.upgrade_required), checked before anything is fetched. Scoped to the organization in the path and audited.

item.name: Discover where an address signs in (public)

request.name: Discover where an address signs in (public)

description.content: Home-realm discovery: says whether an email address signs in through its organization's identity provider, and through which connections. It is judged by the address's domain alone, so every address on a domain gets the same answer whether or not it has an account. sso is true when the organization that verified the domain (or the closest verified domain above it) has switched sso_enabled on for it and has an active SAML, LDAP or OpenID Connect connection; those addresses' own sign-in methods are then refused with 403 auth.sso_required, except for the organization's break-glass members. Each connection gives login_path, below the API's address: a browser goes to it for SAML and OpenID Connect (method redirect), and the directory login name and password are posted to it for LDAP (method credentials). The hosted login adds return_to to a redirect, and posts a credentials connection's sign-in to session_path, which answers with the hosted-login session. An address that is not routed answers sso false with no connections. Unauthenticated; rate-limited like sign-in.

Begins a sign-in through an OpenID Connect connection: it records the sign-in's state, PKCE verifier (S256) and nonce, sets an HttpOnly cookie binding the sign-in to this browser, and redirects the browser to the provider's authorization endpoint, which must be https, asking for the connection's scopes. The provider sends the browser back to GET /v1/oidc-connections/{id}/callback. Only an active connection signs anyone in: a draft one answers 403 oidc_connection.connection_draft and a disabled one 403 oidc_connection.connection_disabled. A provider that can't be reached answers 502 oidc_connection.provider_unreachable; a discovery document that can't be used, or whose issuer isn't the connection's (unless it serves many organizations and the connection lists those it accepts), 500 oidc_connection.misconfigured. The organization's plan must include enterprise SSO (402 billing.upgrade_required). Unauthenticated.

For a sign-in started on the hosted login, where the browser goes back to once it's signed in (the application's authorize request): a path, or an absolute URL on an allowed origin (400 oidc_connection.return_to_invalid otherwise). The provider's answer then returns to the hosted login's /sign-in with the one-time code in the URL fragment, for POST /v1/oidc-connections/session.
(Required)

Where the provider sends the browser back; register it as the connection's redirect URI. The state is spent whatever happens next, and an unknown, spent or expired one answers 400 oidc_connection.state_invalid. A sign-in completes only in the browser that began it, holding the cookie the login call set (403 oidc_connection.other_browser). A refusal by the provider (an error parameter) answers 401 oidc_connection.provider_refused. Otherwise the code is traded at the provider's token endpoint with the PKCE verifier (502 oidc_connection.token_exchange_failed) and the ID token is validated: its signature against the provider's published keys (fetched again once for a key not yet seen), an asymmetric algorithm, iss equal to the connection's issuer (or, for a provider serving many tenants, the issuer of a tid the connection lists), aud naming the client (and azp the client when it names several), exp and iat within a minute's skew, and the nonce this sign-in sent; any failure answers 401 oidc_connection.id_token_invalid. The subject (issuer and sub) is linked to the connection, so another connection asserting it signs nobody in. A linked subject signs in while the organization is still its account's home (403 oidc_connection.user_organization_mismatch). An address not yet linked is adopted or given an account only on a domain the organization has verified (403 oidc_connection.email_domain_unverified), and not when the provider's email_verified is false (403 oidc_connection.email_unverified); a provider that doesn't say (Microsoft Entra ID) is trusted for those domains. An adopted account must have the organization as its home and a verified address (403 oidc_connection.account_unverified), and one that owns or administers the organization is never adopted by its address (403 oidc_connection.account_administers). A suspended account is refused. Every refusal is audited as auth.sign_in_failed with the error code as its reason. On success the browser goes to the console's /sso/callback with a one-time code in the fragment (#oidc_code=...), to trade at POST /v1/oidc-connections/exchange. The plan is checked again when the answer arrives, so one that has since lapsed signs no one in (402 billing.upgrade_required). Once the state is found to be this browser's, a refusal of a sign-in the hosted login began redirects instead to the hosted login's /sign-in with a generic error (sso, or account_inactive for a suspended or deleted account) and its return_to; the refusal is still audited. Unauthenticated.
(Required)

Trades the one-time login code an OpenID Connect sign-in handed the console for a Qeet access and refresh token pair in the connection's organization, while the connection is still active. The code is single-use (401 oidc_connection.login_code_used) and lasts five minutes (401 oidc_connection.login_code_expired); an unknown one answers 401 oidc_connection.login_code_invalid and none 400 oidc_connection.login_code_required. The organization's login hook and address rules apply. Unauthenticated; sent with Cache-Control: no-store.
no-store: the response carries a token, a secret or a sign-in session, so no cache may keep it. (This can only be one of no-store)
no-cache, the same instruction for HTTP/1.0 caches. (This can only be one of no-cache)

Trades the one-time login code a hosted-login OpenID Connect sign-in came back with (the hosted login's /sign-in URL fragment, oidc_code) for the hosted-login session, as POST /v1/auth/session answers: the qe_ls cookie and the user's id. The code is single-use and short-lived (401 oidc_connection.login_code_invalid, oidc_connection.login_code_used or oidc_connection.login_code_expired). The organization's network rules apply (403 auth.address_not_allowed), and an account that is not active is refused (403 auth.account_inactive). As the console's sign-in through a connection, no second factor is asked. The session is recorded as an oidc sign-in. Unauthenticated; CSRF-checked.

item.description: LDAP / Active Directory connection management and bind authentication.

description.content: POST /ldap/{id}/authenticate for the hosted login: the same checks, answered as POST /v1/auth/session is, with the hosted-login session cookie (qe_ls) and the user's id, or the challenge to complete first at POST /v1/auth/session/mfa. Mounted at the root, not under /v1, and unauthenticated; CSRF-checked.
(Required)

Signs a person in with their directory username and password and answers with a token pair, or with a challenge to complete at POST /v1/auth/mfa as for a password sign-in. The connection's organization's network rules apply first (403 auth.address_not_allowed, whatever the password), then the password is checked by a bind against the connection's directory, under the sign-in lockout, login hook, risk and second-factor rules of that organization, as a password sign-in is. The lockout counts a username case-insensitively, ignoring extra spaces. A wrong username or password is refused with 401 ldap.invalid_credentials and counted by the lockout like a wrong password. A locked account answers 429 auth.account_locked whatever the password (a throttled source network, 429 too_many_requests), and when the lockout counters cannot be read or written the sign-in is refused with 503 auth.sign_in_unavailable. A disabled connection is refused with 403 ldap.connection_disabled, and a draft one, still being set up, with 403 ldap.connection_draft; one whose organization's plan no longer includes LDAP is refused with 402 billing.upgrade_required, before the directory is asked. A sign-in that needs another step (a second factor, setting one up, or a risk confirmation by an emailed code) answers with that challenge, as POST /v1/auth/login does; the session it completes is recorded as an ldap_mfa sign-in. A directory account whose email belongs to an account outside the connection's organization is refused with 403 ldap.account_not_in_organization, and an account that is not active with 403 auth.account_inactive. An empty username or password is refused with 400 ldap.credentials_required, and a connection that does not verify the directory's certificate with 422 ldap.tls_verify_required. The account signed in must have the connection's organization as its home (403 ldap.account_not_in_organization), and an existing one adopted by email a verified address, or one the organization's directory provisioned (SCIM), which is then marked verified (403 ldap.account_unverified otherwise). A directory entry is linked to the connection that bound it. An address not yet linked is adopted or given an account only on a domain the organization has verified (the most specific verified domain decides, 403 ldap.email_domain_unverified otherwise), and an account that owns the organization or holds any permission there but the reads organization.read, user.read, role.read, group.read, connection.read, apikey.read, webhook.read, billing.read, policy.read, audit.read and analytics.read is not adopted by its address (403 ldap.account_administers): it keeps its own credentials. A new account is created only while the domain that manages the address has jit_enabled on; otherwise an address with no account is refused with 403 ldap.jit_not_allowed and nothing is created. Existing members are adopted either way. Every sign-in then brings the account in step with the directory, each change audited: its display name; its address, when the directory's is on a domain the organization has verified, is no other account's, and the account doesn't administer the organization (recovery links sent to the old address then stop working); and its groups, as GET /v1/organizations/{organizationID}/ldap/{id}/group-mappings describes.
(Required)

Lists the group mappings of an LDAP connection in the organization. Each maps a group the directory gives the person (idp_group, compared ignoring case) to one of the organization's groups. The groups are the values of the connection's directory mapping targeting groups when it has one (with its transform, such as extracting the CN), else of the entry's memberOf. At every sign-in through the connection the person joins the groups those reach, through these mappings or as the external id of a group SCIM provisioned, and leaves the groups the connection's sign-ins put them in that they no longer reach. A membership an administrator or SCIM made is never changed, and a group whose roles carry the owner role or an administrative permission (any but the reads organization.read, user.read, role.read, group.read, connection.read, apikey.read, webhook.read, billing.read, policy.read, audit.read and analytics.read) is never joined: sign-in takes out anyone it put there. Maps a group the directory gives the person (a memberOf DN, or the value the connection's groups mapping makes of it) to one of the organization's groups, from each person's next sign-in. Whoever maps a group hands out what it grants: the caller must hold every permission the group's roles carry, as adding a member needs (403 rbac.grant_exceeds_caller, or rbac.owner_only for a group holding the owner role). Qeet ID — Developer API (keys, webhooks, secrets, agents)

Non-human identities and developer integrations for Qeet ID — API keys, AI agents, webhooks, auth hooks, vaults, and verifiable credentials.

## The non-human identity model

- **API keys** resolve to actor_type `api_key`.
- **Service principals** (defined in the Federation API) resolve to actor_type `service`.
- **AI agents** resolve to actor_type `agent`.

## Start here

1. Create an **API key** for simple machine access (`Authorization: ApiKey <key>`), or register an **agent** for AI workloads.
2. **Agent tokens are re-minted, never refreshed** — call the mint endpoint again to obtain a fresh short-lived token.
3. Wire up **webhooks** and **auth hooks** to react to events and customize auth flows.
4. Store secrets in the **Secrets Vault** (organization secrets) or connect third-party accounts via the **Token Vault** (external OAuth credentials, refreshed for you).

## Authentication

Auth modes: `bearerAuth` (user/service JWT), `apiKeyAuth` (`Authorization: ApiKey <key>` — legacy scheme), `scimBearer` (per-organization SCIM token), `clientCredentials` (OAuth M2M), and `ssoCookie` (hosted-login SSO session). CSRF protection applies only to cookie sessions (`ssoCookie`): requests authorised by `bearerAuth` or `apiKeyAuth` bypass it, as do the token endpoint (POST /v1/oauth/token) and the directory sign-in (POST /ldap/{id}/authenticate), which carry their credentials in the request. Basic credentials do not bypass it. A request that fails the check is refused with 403 `csrf_failed`.

The responses of the token vault's access-token read, and of the operations returning a new API key, agent or webhook secret, a revealed secret or an issued credential, are sent with `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`.

Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header naming the request; quote it when reporting a problem. An error body repeats it as `error.request_id`. A path with an encoded slash or backslash (`%2F`, `%5C`) is refused with 400 `bad_request`.

## Related APIs

- **Authentication & Access API** — login, passkeys, MFA, authorization
- **Identity Management API** — organizations, users, groups, invitations
- **Federation API** — OIDC/OAuth provider, SAML, SCIM, LDAP, social
- **Operations API** — audit, analytics, billing

## Contract maintenance

This document covers routes mounted by internal/bootstrap/router.go. internal/bootstrap/openapi_coverage_test.go walks the production mount helpers and fails when a mounted operation is undocumented, a documented operation is stale, or API-auth security declarations disagree with runtime classification.

item.name: API Keys
item.description: Long-lived API keys for machine access.

description.content: Creates a long-lived API key for machine access. The plaintext key is returned only once at creation and is never retrievable again, so store it securely. Its name is required (422 apikey.name_required) and at most 200 characters (422 validation_failed on name). Callers present it as `Authorization: ApiKey <key>` and resolve to actor_type `api_key`. A user_id, if sent, must be the caller's own: a key can act only for the person who creates it (403 apikey.user_not_self otherwise). Such a personal key works only while that person's account is active: it is refused while they are suspended and once they are deleted. It also does only what that person may do now: a route needs both one of the key's scopes and the person's permission for it (a vault read, their secret.read), so a key loses what its person loses. item.name: Webhooks
item.description: Outbound webhook endpoint management. A subscription names the events it receives, from the event catalogue; an event's name is its version, so an incompatible payload change comes as a new name, while new fields may be added to any payload. Each delivery is a POST whose JSON body is the envelope {id, type, organization_id, occurred_at, data}: id is the same in every delivery of one event, retries included, so deduplicate on it, and data is the event's own payload. Deliveries are at least once and in no guaranteed order. Headers: X-Qeet-Event (the type), X-Qeet-Delivery-ID, X-Qeet-Timestamp (Unix seconds) and X-Qeet-Signature, "sha256=" and the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the subscription's secret, of the timestamp, a ".", and the raw body. For 24 hours after the secret is rotated the header holds two comma-separated values, the new secret's first; accept the delivery if any one matches. Verify in constant time before parsing, and refuse a timestamp more than a few minutes old. Answer 2xx quickly: a network error, a 5xx, 408 or 429 is retried with jittered backoff from 30 seconds up to an hour, for 60 attempts; any other 4xx dead-letters the delivery at once. A dead-lettered delivery stays in the delivery list and can be sent again. A subscription whose deliveries fail for 3 days with no success is disabled (disabled_reason "failing") and the members who hold webhook.write are alerted in-app; deliveries queued meanwhile are sent once it is enabled again.

Qeet ID — Operations API (audit, billing, analytics)

Observability, governance, and commercial operations for Qeet ID.

## Start here

1. **Health** first — `GET /healthz` and `/readyz` need no authentication and are the easiest successful call for a new integrator.
2. **Observe** — activity feed, usage analytics, and universal search.
3. **Investigate & govern** — audit log, compliance evidence, data retention, GDPR erasure, and SIEM log sinks.
4. **Commercial** — billing, plans, and entitlements.

## Authentication

Auth modes: `bearerAuth` (user/service JWT), `apiKeyAuth` (`Authorization: ApiKey <key>` — legacy scheme), `scimBearer` (per-organization SCIM token), `clientCredentials` (OAuth M2M), and `ssoCookie` (hosted-login SSO session). CSRF protection applies only to cookie sessions (`ssoCookie`): requests authorised by `bearerAuth` or `apiKeyAuth` bypass it, as do the token endpoint (POST /v1/oauth/token) and the directory sign-in (POST /ldap/{id}/authenticate), which carry their credentials in the request. Basic credentials do not bypass it. A request that fails the check is refused with 403 `csrf_failed`.

Responses that carry a token, a sign-in session or a newly created secret are sent with `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`; no operation in this API returns one.

Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header naming the request; quote it when reporting a problem. An error body repeats it as `error.request_id`. A path with an encoded slash or backslash (`%2F`, `%5C`) is refused with 400 `bad_request`.

## Related APIs

- **Authentication & Access API** — login, passkeys, MFA, authorization
- **Identity Management API** — organizations, users, groups, invitations
- **Federation API** — OIDC/OAuth provider, SAML, SCIM, LDAP, social
- **Developer API** — API keys, agents, webhooks, vaults

## Contract maintenance

This document covers routes mounted by internal/bootstrap/router.go. internal/bootstrap/openapi_coverage_test.go walks the production mount helpers and fails when a mounted operation is undocumented, a documented operation is stale, or API-auth security declarations disagree with runtime classification.

item.description: Liveness, readiness, and Prometheus metrics.

description.content: Returns 200 whenever the process can answer the request, reporting only that the instance is running rather than that its dependencies are reachable. Requires no authentication and performs no dependency checks, making it the cheapest way to confirm connectivity. Container orchestrators use this signal to decide whether to restart the instance.

Exposes process and request metrics in Prometheus exposition format for scraping by a metrics collector. The scraper presents METRICS_TOKEN as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; without the right token the endpoint answers 404, as it does everywhere but development when no METRICS_TOKEN is set, since its counters (sign-in throttles among them) would tell an attacker how close they are to a limit. The payload reflects the instance's current counters and gauges at the time of the call.

Runs every registered dependency probe under a short shared timeout and returns 200 only when all pass, otherwise 503 with a per-check breakdown (ok or fail; the cause is logged, never answered). Requires no authentication. Unlike the liveness probe, a failure here indicates the instance is temporarily unable to serve traffic, so orchestrators route requests away without restarting the process.

Answers what is running on this instance: the release version, the commit it was built from and its build date, and the database migration the instance runs on next to the newest migration the build carries. Requires no authentication and reads nothing at request time (the migration is the one found at start). Operators compare it with the deploy record after a deploy or rollback.

Opens a Server-Sent Events stream of ActivityEvent frames for the caller's organization: the audit records themselves, every kind (sign-ins and MFA included), each with its own audit id, so a live event can be opened and related like one from the history. The server follows the audit log every two seconds, or at once when the organization acts. Each frame is `id: <cursor>\nevent: activity\ndata: <json>\n\n`; periodic `: keep-alive` comments prevent proxy timeouts.

When `Last-Event-ID` is supplied (the `id` of the last frame received, an opaque cursor, not the event's UUID) the server replays every audit event newer than it, in chronological order, before switching to the live stream. One connection replays at most 1,000 audit rows: further behind, it sends the cursor of the last row read and a `retry:` frame and ends, and the client's reconnect carries on from there. A frame may carry only an `id` (no event): the cursor of rows the filters passed over, kept as the client's Last-Event-ID. A live frame's id sits ten seconds before its event, to cover records whose transaction committed late; the stream sends each record once, and a reconnect may repeat one, recognisable by its id. Delivery is at least once: a reconnect may repeat an event but doesn't skip one, and a client too slow for the live stream is sent a `retry:` frame and disconnected, to catch up from the audit log on reconnect.

The stream lasts only as long as the access it was opened with. It ends when the access token or API key expires, and within 30 seconds of the reader losing access: their session ended, audit.read no longer theirs (or no longer the key's), the API key revoked, the service principal or agent disabled. It also ends if that check can't be made. A new request is then refused as any other would be.

Server-side filters (`?types`, `?severity`, `?category`) are applied to both the replay and the live stream. The connection organization is derived from the JWT principal only — never from the URL or body.

The write deadline is extended to 1 hour. Set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` is already set by the server (Nginx/Caddy proxy buffering disabled).

item.name: GDPR
item.description: Right-to-erasure purge requests.

description.content: Requests erasure of a person's account, carried out after the grace period unless cancelled. The erasure ends their sessions, redacts the account (email, phone, name, avatar, external ID and metadata) and deletes everything else it left: credentials and second factors, sign-in history, sessions and remembered devices, linked social and single sign-on accounts, application consents and grants, connected accounts and their tokens, personal API keys, role, group and break-glass memberships, application assignments and the persistent identifiers applications know them by, directory profiles, notifications, sign-in links and failed sign-in counters, and the payloads of the person's data exports; verifiable credentials issued to them are revoked and their claims cleared. The audit trail and the request itself are kept; the request goes on naming the account by user_id after the account is deleted for good. Requires gdpr.write. Held to the rule for deleting the account: nobody erases someone who outranks them (403 rbac.target_is_owner for an owner, unless the caller is one, or 403 rbac.target_outranks_caller).

item.name: Send a message / continue with tool results (SSE stream)

request.name: Send a message / continue with tool results (SSE stream)

description.content:
Opens a streaming turn of the AI qeetai conversation. The response is a `text/event-stream` of SSE frames (thinking, token, tool_call, tool_result, error, done). Each frame is `event: <type>\ndata: <json>\n\n`.

On `stop_reason=tool_use` the stream ends with `done{reason:"tool_use"}`; the browser executes the tool under its own bearer token and posts `tool_results` to this same endpoint to continue generation. Only the tools the model is offered (read-only in this version) are sent as `tool_call` frames: a call to any other tool is dropped, recorded as `qeetai.tool.refused` and noted in the reply's text.

Requires `QEETAI_PROVIDER` configured server-side; returns `409 qeetai_unconfigured` otherwise.

A conversation answers one turn at a time: a message while its previous turn is still running, on any instance, is refused with `409 qeetai.turn_in_progress` (retryable) and not stored. A turn sends the model only the conversation's latest 40 messages, within 256 KiB, from a message of the user's, so earlier ones are left out; a turn whose own messages are larger ends with an `error` frame of code `history_too_long` (start a new conversation). A reply longer than 64 KiB is cut there and kept, as at the model's own token limit. A turn runs for at most 10 minutes.
(Required)

description.content: Returns a hosted-payment URL to redirect the admin to, or {status:"active"} when the plan is free or no card provider serves the request (direct activation). The provider is chosen by billing country (config-driven; an omitted country falls back to currency-based routing: INR → Razorpay, else the default provider). The provider's webhook later activates the subscription. When invoice tax is configured, it is worked out from the billing profile (or, when the profile names no country, from country) before the payment opens, and the provider charges the total, tax included; the paid invoice shows that charge. A plan activated directly by invoice-only billing gets an open invoice; a free plan a paid zero one. Send an Idempotency-Key header to retry it safely: a retry with the same key and body within 24 hours gets the first answer, marked Idempotent-Replayed: true; the same key with another body answers 422 idempotency.key_reused, one still being processed 409 idempotency.in_progress, and one whose first request stopped before answering 409 idempotency.outcome_unknown: check whether it took effect, then retry with a new key.
(Required) The organization's ID. On an authenticated route it must be the organization of the caller's credential: another is refused with 403, and a value that is not a UUID with 400.

Returns the organization's subscription. A trial grants its plan until trial_end, and a plan marked to cancel until current_period_end. Any other plan renews at current_period_end: a free one starts its next period, and a paid one is billed with an open renewal invoice and turns past_due, keeping its plan for the payment grace (7 days unless configured) while that invoice is paid, through POST /v1/organizations/{organizationID}/billing/invoices/{invoiceID}/pay or by bank transfer. description.content: Begins a hosted payment for a plan chosen during signup, before any organization exists. The organization is created only once payment completes, so an abandoned checkout never leaves a dangling organization. Scoped to the authenticated user; the organization name and slug are required and the return URLs must be valid absolute URLs. Returns the details needed to redirect the browser to the payment provider. When invoice tax is configured, the provider charges the total tax included, taxed by the billing country given, and the new organization's paid invoice shows that charge.

Completes a checkout from a Razorpay payment-link redirect using the signed callback parameters posted by the browser. Authenticity is established by the Razorpay signature rather than a session, so the endpoint requires no authentication and is CSRF-exempt. Completion is idempotent, so a later asynchronous webhook for the same payment is a harmless no-op.

description.content: Returns the organization's resolved entitlements: the effective plan code, the boolean feature flags, and the numeric limits (-1 = unlimited). Resolved from the active subscription (falling back to the organization's plan label), so an in-app upgrade is reflected immediately. A subscription grants its plan only until current_period_end (a trial until trial_end): nothing renews it, so after that the organization has the free plan's entitlements until it pays again. Readable by any authenticated member of the organization; scoped to the caller's own organization. audit_retention_days is enforced: once a day, the organization's audit events older than that are deleted (all but the newest, its chain kept verifiable) and the deletion is recorded as audit.events_purged; -1 keeps them all.
(Required) The organization's ID. On an authenticated route it must be the organization of the caller's credential: another is refused with 403, and a value that is not a UUID with 400.

description.content: Returns the organization's current consumption for each metered resource, such as seats, applications, and API keys, for display against the plan's limits. seats counts the people holding a role in the organization, directly or through a group that carries one, each once, plus its pending invitations; an account holding no role, such as a customer signing in to the organization's applications, holds no seat. mau counts the people active in the organization so far this calendar month (UTC): each person who signed in to it, or renewed a session in it, at least once, counted once. API keys, service principals and AI agents are not counted. It complements the entitlements endpoint, which resolves the plan's capability set, by running the underlying count queries only when the usage view needs them.
